item.title: Shepherd boy: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
► my detailed thoughts◄
- close

SCP-XXXX is to be stored in Containment Area M21 located in 300m underground of the Gobi desert in Mongolia.

Delete that second “in” (right before 300m)

SCP-XXXX is to be held in a 5 m cube made of entirely Tungsten metal, with no gap for organic life to enter.

Why does it matter that the cube be Five meters in length/widtch/height? What if it were 4.98 meters? Would that invalidate the containment? This is why specific measurements of containment chambers is mostly avoided these days.

If any entities that reside in SCP-XXXX-1 move from their position, they are to be immediately apprehended and interrogated before being held in a cell with same containment procedure as SCP-CXXX.

Suggest: Entities residing in SCP-XXXX-1 that move from their position, are to be apprehended, interrogated, and remanded to a containment cell under equivalent containment procedures as SCP-XXXX.

No more than five personnel wearing Hazmat suits, are to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at the same time. Its activity is to be monitored 24/7 and no unauthorized personnel and civilian are to be in the proximity of the area or enter SCP-XXXX-1.

Suggest: A maximum of five hazmat protected personnel are permitted to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at any given time. Access to SCP-XXXX-1 is restricted to security cleared personnel.

In the event of a Containment Breach, all on site researchers and personnel are to evacuate immediately or stay in shelter until the MTF Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) arrive at the facility and apprehended the entity.

Suggest: In the event of a containment breach, all on-site personnel are to evacuate or shelter in place until such time as MTF-Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) apprehend the entity.

ALSO: which entity? Clarify

SCP-CXXX consists of two components: a cave (SCP-XXXX-1) and humanoid protecting it (SCP-XXXX).

Suggest: SCP-XXXX consists of two interrelated anomalies: a cave, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 and a humanoid entity guarding the cave, designated as SCP-XXXX.
ALSO: I suggest reversing the designations, the Cave could be the XXXX and the humanoid, -1, because it seems the cave is the central anomaly.

SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sunburn and wears an old dark green Hun area deel1 which been ripped and torn, however, SCP-XXXX refused to change it.

SCP-XXXX has the ability to manifest entities made out of natural components which resemble a Chinese dragon. Entities length is unknown.
So several things, “an old dark green Hun area deel” is confusing… suggest: “SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sun damage and an deteriorating, dark-green Hun deel that the entity refuses to change.” & I don’t know what “made out of natural components” means in this context, so I would clarify.

ALSO: IS this meant to be two paragraphs? If so, there is no spacing between them.

SCP-XXXX-1 is a cave under abandoned Mining factory, it is measured to be around 6 kilometers deep.

Suggest: a cave under an abandoned mining facility, measured to be approximately six kilometers below the surface.

  • There is no such thing as a mining factory, change this everywhere… it’s a facility or just a mine.

However, how big SCP-XXXX-1 mass is impossible to measure. SCP-XXXX-1 resides a snake-like creature approximately 1 kilometers, maybe even bigger.

Suggest: Exact measurements of SCP-XXXX-1’s dimensions have been impossible due to a large serpentine entity, at least one kilometer in length, that resides within the cave.

About fifty kilometers down, there is a massive field stretching further from the human eye, filled with stationary humanoids varies in ages, they're made out of natural components, different species of flowers but growing in the same root. The radio cuts off the moment entering SCP-XXXX-1.

Fifty kilometers down where? I thought you said the cave was 6 km below the surface? What do you mean? Also this is just really awkwardly written.

The investigation into SCP-XXXX-1 and its relation with SCP-XXXX is ongoing.

Cut this. It’s implied because there’s more to read after it.

This is a critique in progress… You have so many awkward phrases and poorly structured sentences… I would sit down and really examine your work here, and see if you can't clean it up without myself or another critter to do so.

Additionally, all the dialogue is stilted and hard to read. Go through it and say each line aloud, then if it sounds awkward try to make it sound more grounded and believable.

item.title: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
Don't think of a bank account as something that has a dollar added to it or subtracted from it ad random. Think of it as a record of transactions, or a closed system of exchanges. Money does not come from nowhere - someone has to be depositing money into those accounts from business entity. This might be a neat use case for Envelope Logistics, if that's a direction you want to take it.

Basically, make sure there's some kind of reasonable path for the consumer to get money. Maybe they get diamonds or processed gold in the mail, or winning lottery tickets, etc.

item.title: Try again? Fugitive vs the Yakuza: Re: Try again? Fugitive vs the Yakuza
item.content:encoded:
Requested to review by Wikidot PM.

+ show block
– hide block

"You here to talk to the boss?"

Personally, I feel like this should be its own separate line.

He smiles when you arrive at his desk.

I can't place my finger on it, but this just seems out of flow for the rest of the interaction. You'd think this guy would smile on first seeing him, or as he was lighting the cigarette.

"Thank you." Tsuyaki leans back in his chair, and lights a cigarette.

"So tell me, how did you get this money?" Tsuyaki blows smoke into your face as he talks.

You could probably combine this into one paragraph: "Thank you." Tsuyaki leans back in his chair, and lights a cigarette. He blows smoke into your face as he continues to talk. "So tell me, how did you get this money?"

"Really? Not many people who come to me have 10,000,000 yen. It's even stranger that a foreigner would." Tsuyaki leans forward.

"So tell me. Did you steal this money?"

Same here.

"No, I don't like having a target on my back." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

"I guess that's why you want me to smuggle you off the island." You remain silent as you wait for your reward.

Yet more weird line breaking. I think it flows better as:

"No, I don't like having a target on my back."

"I guess that's why you want me to smuggle you off the island." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

You remain silent as you wait for your reward.

"Or are you running from the GOC?"

Probably would combine this with the paragraph above it.

Tsuyaki's eyes dart behind you for a brief moment.

Make this separate from the reader's dialogue. At this point, I think you get my drift. Keep Tsuyaki's actions separate from the reader's dialogue, and vice versa. I'm going to stop pointing it out now.

You simultaneously remove your gun, and shoot the right in the chest.

Did you accidentally a word here?

"I would never help you. Traitors deserve to die." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

Yeah, this is some Snidely Whiplash levels of villain dialogue here, my dude. I imagine people who just had a gun fired next to their head are not quite cartoony when they speak.

When the three guards rush around the corner, you begin to open fire. one goes down, as the others duck behind cover, and return fire.

Ending two sentences after another with the same word always parses weird to me. Might want to switch up the vocab for one of these two.

The only survivors of the operation was Roach and fellow
strike team members Echo and Blanket. After review of the

Weird line break here.

All in all, it's a bit of a fun ride through the various iterations of these events. Nothing groundbreaking, but a neat bit of noir-style action. That said, when you get to the personnel file on roach you really break all your flow and momentum to a halt. To be honest, that level of exposition kills the story dead. While it is likely going to be essential info for your overall story arc, I'd say it would be better if you capped off the story and including the file in another piece. But that's just my opinion.

item.title: Explained SCP in need of review: Re: Explained SCP in need of review
item.content:encoded:
It's certainly clever, albeit stretching the use of the 'explained SCP' category.

The core idea has merit and the narrative is quite good. The ending works but I'm a bit let down by the actual explanation of what happens (that being "weird eldritch things"). I don't know if that because of a preconceived notion that -EX articles need to be fully explainable or because it feels like a cop out.

I think this article is 85% of the way there, and would be well-served by a purely non-anomalous rationale for Thompson's defection - e.g. bureaucratic reasons.

item.title: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
I have very mixed feelings about this. The core ideal is fine, but I'm morally obligated to point out that compulsion should be avoided.

The first two logs are good. The third is entirely too wordy and I think breaks the suspension of disbelief - O5 should have more control over itself and realize exactly what is happening - not break down into disorder and infighting.

The description is greatly improved but there's still a massive dangling thread in that 'bank account money' comes out of thin air, which can't really happen with such a computerized banking system we have today. I think there's room for cleverness in handling that can add verisimilitude to what is admittedly a rather wacky article. The asteroid bit is also entirely extraneous and I'm not sure what its purpose is.

The writing is certainly better than the original article, but I think I would still no vote. The logs add a lot but my opinion is soured by the third log. The ending still works as it did in the original article. As a rewrite, I think you're still a bit hamstrung by the original core idea and I'm not sure there's much that can be done to mitigate that without changing the article fundamentally.

item.title: Draft "Disconnected Restroom": Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this.

I took a quick look at the draft. There are a lot of simple errors, such as lack of correct paragraph spacing, unnecessary crossed-out materials in the containment (try to avoid redacting or withdrawing anything in that section; if you really must include earlier versions of containment, I recommend having an archived version in a collapsible), and inconsistent section heading capitalization. The containment procedures are rather disorganized as well; try to group similar information together rather than having it all sort of scattered and in need of clear flow/transition between topics.

Address these issues first and let me know when you have done so; I will then provide a full review of the draft.

item.title: Need critiques!: Forum Criticism Team - Moderator Post
item.content:encoded:
Atreum, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: SCP Draft: The Place I Belong: Re: SCP Draft: The Place I Belong
item.content:encoded:
Hey, Grig! I'll take a look for ya!

Just know that my clinical tone is meh, but I'm a lot better with dialogue.

Alrighty.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Disinformation campaigns are to be spearheaded to label SCP-XXXX-A as a UNESCO World Friendship and Peace Village to draw in more tourism.

The fact that a ConProc demands more attention is already weird enough to draw me in.
I dig it.

SCP-XXXX is a series of anomalous dreams that can occur in a certain segment of the population of Europe and Asia: most often creatives and individuals who attest to feeling at odds with society.

I feel personally called out here and I'm not sure how to mentally process this.

I just finished the Description and I don't really have any qualms with it. The dream sequences reminds me heavily of the River Styx and Charon, something I'm not sure if you did on purpose or not.
Either way, no clinical issues so far.

Aside from this:

genius loci

Did you mean 'genus'?

A little confused on that bit. I had to Google 'loci' and it gave me stuff about genetics and mathematics, neither of which this piece seems to be going for. I…actually no clue what this bit is supposed to show.

I'm normally not a fan of free verse (that is what that poetry style is, right?), but the poem written by Tefvik is wonderfully done and the allusions to the hooded figure in the SCP-XXXX dreams is also nicely done.

Especially 'blessed be the stones of your dreaming streets.'

prototypical oneirosensory visualization recording device.

Ironic…we're both currently drafting something that headcanons pioneering dream-recording Foundation tech.

I…don't know how to process this either.

I do think this is great headcanon, and I think your method of wording this is a lot better and a lot more developed than mine.

Dr. Rossi has confirmed that she is experiencing SCP-XXXX events and has been periodically for the previous three weeks.

We can clean this up and shorten it into, 'Dr. Rossi has confirmed that she has been periodically experiencing SCP-XXXX events for the previous three weeks.'

[ Initial view is of a mist shrouded body of water, which appears to be a river. The night is dark, with only a crescent moon serving as illumination.]

Unnecessary extra space before 'Initial' and after the bracket.

[The boat has stopped directly in front of subject in a manner inconsistent with the flowing water of the river, as if being held in place. The figure extends his arm out with an open palm.]

I love dream logic. This is a lovely detail to show how unearthly this place is. Other than, you know, the weird hooded figure, the mist and—
You know what I mean.

Sixteen minutes of footage are lost due to technical failure.

Both of our headcanoned dream-recording technology also involves significant lapses in dream recording to simulate the feeling of actual dream timeline-logic.

That's…frighteningly coincidental.

I love it. Love it, love it, love it <3

[Subject is within the village, walking down its streets. The stone buildings resemble architecture from the 18the century

There's an extra 'e' in '18th'

Rossi: The air is chilly, like an early spring night but not so cold as to be uncomfortable. Significant moisture in the air, consistent with misty conditions. The river in front of me is jet black, I cannot tell how deep it is by eye. I –”

This is very prose-y instead of diaogue-y (if that makes sense), but this is a dream and we could say she is trying to ground herself in a world where normal logic doesn't function.

[Sounds of a scuffle and Rossi cursing loudly cursing.]

Two 'cursing's here.

Removing either would fix it, funny enough.

Many instances8 of SCP-XXXX-1 are seen lining the square and staring at subject.]

There has been no mention of SCP-XXXX-1 up until this point, so I don't know what they're supposed to be.

Subject stands in a town square, the cobble stones shifting beneath her feet.

I absolutely adore the usage of dream logic and dream visuals here.

Answers don’t come in dreams at least not for you.

Comma after 'dreams'. Unless you're going for a sort of mysterious thing where the run on sentences show how unearthly this being is.

Also, odd how its dialogue switches to a different, bolded and italcized style here wheras earlier, it spoke like this.

Also, earlier, it was addressed as Unknown, whereas here, there's no addressing as such.

Maybe I'm just a stickler for consistency, I don't know, but I found this a tad jarring.

Wrong

No period.

Rossi: What are you talking about?

I personally imagine this character responding with 'What you do mean 'wrong?'' as a way to sass it. Can't explain why.

I just finished the first Addendum.

Hmmm…so far, I find the dialogue pretty decent. There's a good sense of mystery and a good sense of buildup, but I don't feel attached to Rossi. She feels like she's just there.

Also, the hooded figure feels a little too 'generic mysterious dream person' to me.

Like, I really dig it all, but it's missing a little bit of that pizzazz which makes me go from nodding my head and approving to making the following face:

:o

And losing all breath at the insane BS occuring before me.

Descriptions are lovely, though and the use of dream logic is very good. A little too downplayed, though, in my opinion; it's a dream and yet, despite lapses in timeline and everything being misty and hard to make out with shadowy figures, it doesn't get weird enough in my opinion. The weirdest we see is the dream figure levitating and twirling in the air. It's a dream and I think the surreal nature can be cranked up a notch or 12.

Then again, I can see that that isn't what you're really going for, so this part can be taken however you wish.

Personally, I just love seeing dream logic become as surreal and weird as possible. Probably just me.

11. There is no body of water within twenty kilometers of Kayaköy.

I like this touch here to show the difference between the 'real' version and the dream version.

Waltham: I can get to the edge of town, it’s not infinite… but then I’ll blank and it will fold in on itself; fall apart until it reforms and I’m sent right back to the fucking church..

Lovely dream logic. Sorry I'm being a broken record, I just really love weird things.

Waltham: I’m not alone here. I thought I was, but I’m not. There’s something here. I haven’t seen anything but… I’m being watched.

This feels a tad too rehearsed.

Waltham: I'll be the judge of that. I said, come out where I can see you.

You are looking right at me. Do you like it?

Needs a space between the two.

The street and buildings are also exhibiting non-Euclidean geometrics as they fold in upon themselves, shifting the camera between different elevations and rapidly restructuring from one layout to another.

This. I personally would like more stuff like this. That said, I'm having a difficult time imagining all of this. Then again, describing non-euclidean geometry is very difficult, so I'm not really sure what else to offer here.

Personally, this makes me think of the video game Control when I imagine the walls moving. Same with the streets.

Do you like it this way?

[Waltham does not respond. She is believed to be unconscious.]

Oh.

So the thing has a clumsy side. I…don't really like this scene. To me, this moment feels almost Tom and Jerry-ish in a piece that's meant to feel melancholy and strange.

And there’s no one else… You have to stay!

This was the twist that gave me chills.

After her debriefing, the current Special Containment Procedures were put in place. To date, no further SCP-XXXX events have occurred.

Well, shit. The hooded figure is just lonely and wants company. Well, that's a twist I wasn't expecting.

Other than that last bit, a good bit of the scenes just felt really rehearsed. The sequence of events were intriguing enough to keep me going and it was built up well and the dialogue was serviceable, but I think I can just summarize it as that:serviceable.

The twist? Fantastic.

I can understand the clumsy moment earlier now. The child-like clinginess and that clumsy moment from earlier, the way it begs for people to stay. It's like a lonely little kid that just wants friends.

That's a great twist.

I just think the journey along the way needs to be patched up.

Rossi and Waltham just feel like vehicles to show some weird stuff happenng.

I get the feeling that Rossi is meant to be sassy and strongwilled while Waltham is supposed to be serious and soldier-tough with a soft side, but if that's what you were going for, it doesn't come through enough.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day, Grig!

<3

If you got any questions or I was clumsy and was unclear on a few things, feel free to PM or .tell me!
